_README.purpose: Which statement TEMPLATE a filer's numbers should be read against. Drives the per-regime overrides in configs/fundamentals/fundamentals_kpis.json and the expected-absence register in configs/fundamentals/fundamentals_exceptions.json.
_README.primary_signal: THE FILER'S OWN STATEMENT ROLE URI. A filer that presents a deposit-based balance sheet has told us it is a bank, in its own filing, for that period. That is evidence; a GICS label is a third-party classification applied to the whole company today and back-dated over its entire history.
_README.tiebreak_signal: GICS, from sp500_tickers (sector / industry_group / sub_industry), used ONLY when no role URI matches -- older filings and small filers often ship no recognisable role.
_README.why_role_uri_first: GICS routes a company; a role URI routes a FILING. A company that changed business mix (or was reclassified) keeps one GICS label across a history in which its statements genuinely changed shape.
resolution: 1. Match the filing's presentation role URIs against `role_patterns` below. First regime with a match wins, in the declared order.
2. Otherwise match GICS `sub_industry`, then `industry_group`, then `sector`, against each regime's `gics` block -- most specific first.
`exceptions.force_regime` overrides BOTH, by sub_industry, and is how the Article-5 fee businesses are kept out of the financial templates.
_README.measured_on: sp500_tickers, 491 tickers, read 2026-08-21. Every ticker list below is the LIVE membership, not an illustration.

bank.description: Deposit-taking lender. Unclassified balance sheet, net-revenue top line, capex not reconstructible.
bank.role_note: `sfp-dbo` = Statement of Financial Position, Deposit Based Operations (FASB role 108000). `soi-int` (132001) is the interest-based statement of income; `scf-dbo` (160000) the deposit-based cash flow.
bank.consumer_finance_note: Card issuers and consumer lenders are routed here because they present a lender's statements, not because GICS calls them Financial Services. AXP is the already-confirmed case: its total revenue runs the 'net of interest expense' convention while its netIncome and totalAssets tie to an external source at 0.000% on the same rows.

insurer.description: Underwriter. Premiums-plus-investment-income top line; insurance contracts are scoped out of ASC 606.
insurer.role_note: `sfp-ibo` = Statement of Financial Position, Insurance Based Operations (108200); `soi-ins` the insurance statement of income (136000).

regime_break.reason: long-duration contract measurement changed, so insurer equity and reserve-linked lines step at adoption.

insurer.insurance_brokers_excluded: Insurance Brokers are NOT here -- see exceptions.force_regime. A broker earns commission, holds no reserves and files an Article 5 statement.

broker_dealer.description: Securities-based operations. Unclassified balance sheet, trading-revenue top line.
broker_dealer.role_note: `sfp-sbo` = Statement of Financial Position, Securities Based Operations (112000).
broker_dealer.note: GS's capex uses a narrower financial-sector definition than an industrial's -- already a confirmed known-definitional-difference case against external sources.

real_estate.description: Property owner/lessor. Often an unclassified balance sheet; rental top line; Up-C and operating-partnership structures are common.
real_estate.role_note: `sfp-clreo` / `sfp-ucreo` = classified / unclassified Real Estate Operations (110000 / 110200); `soi-reit` the REIT statement of income (145000).
real_estate._roster_correction: PLD (Prologis, Industrial REITs) was MISSING from this roster until 2026-08-21, giving 23 entries where the live membership is 24. The absence register's arithmetic was unaffected -- its real_estate._n of 19 already counted PLD among the 24 candidates minus 5 with no facts -- but this file's README calls these lists 'the LIVE membership, not an illustration', so the gap was real. It is also the single most predictable omission available: Industrial REITs (GICS 601025) is the sub-industry the first research already flagged as the one a contiguous-code-range scan silently drops, which is why this file matches sub-industry NAMES instead.
real_estate.not_contiguous_note: The equity-REIT sub-industry set is NOT one contiguous GICS block -- Industrial REITs sits apart from the residential/retail run. Matching a code RANGE silently drops it. This config therefore matches sub-industry NAMES, which is also what sp500_tickers actually stores.
real_estate.entity_scope_note: Up-C / operating-partnership filers scope the LP along `LegalEntityAxis`, frequently with a COMPANY-EXTENSION member (MAA uses `maa:LimitedPartnershipMember`). Filter on the AXIS, never on a fixed member list.

utility.description: Rate-regulated utility. Regulated-revenue top line, regulatory assets, AFUDC-equity in income.
utility.role_patterns_note: Utilities rarely ship a distinctive FASB role; GICS is the practical signal here and the role list is deliberately weak rather than invented.
utility.multi_registrant_note: A utility holding company files ONE instance covering several registrant CIKs -- Southern Company carries six, with 3,579 `LegalEntityAxis` occurrences and all identifiers set to the parent. Consolidated (default-member) facts only.

energy.description: Oil and gas. Article 5 statements, but a distinctive revenue root and a depletion-bearing D&A line.
energy.note: Not a FASB template regime -- it exists because the revenue ROOT varies (`Revenues` for XOM, `RevenuesAndOther` for APA) and because depletion makes `DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization` the only correct D&A aggregate. Both are handled by reading the linkbase, so this regime mostly carries the expected-absence profile.

industrial.description: The DEFAULT template: Article 5 classified balance sheet, Rule 5-03 income statement.
industrial.note: Anything with no matching role and no more specific GICS match lands here. That is correct: Article 5 IS the general rule, and the other regimes are Reg S-X's enumerated specialised-industry exceptions.

hybrid.description: A conglomerate whose single statement genuinely spans several templates.
hybrid.note: Berkshire underwrites insurance, owns a railroad and runs an equity book from one balance sheet. Forcing it into any one template produces a confidently wrong number, so it is EXCLUDED from regime-relative scoring rather than classified. Its absolute values are still extracted.

force_regime._why: The four verified GICS traps. Each of these sits inside a financial-sector GICS block but files ARTICLE 5 statements -- a fee business with revenue, cost of revenue and a classified balance sheet. Routing GICS sector 'Financials' wholesale to a bank or insurer template is the single largest classification error available here, and it would hit 36 live tickers (Insurance Brokers 6 + Financial Exchanges & Data 9 + Transaction & Payment Processing 9 + Asset Management & Custody Banks 12 = 36; an earlier draft of this file said 37, an arithmetic slip in the prose only -- the ticker lists themselves matched the live data exactly).
force_regime._gics_financials_reconciliation: Live query of sp500_tickers WHERE sector = 'Financials' returns 13 sub-industries / 76 tickers, reconciling exactly: bank 16 + insurer 17 + broker_dealer 6 + industrial-via-force_regime 36 + hybrid 1 (BRK-B, Multi-Sector Holdings) = 76. So GICS Financials resolves to FIVE destinations, not four. `hybrid` is a legitimate fifth bucket; it is easy to overlook only because it is explicitly carved out of regime-relative scoring. (Those 16/17 counts are GICS membership; the absence register's per-regime denominators are lower because they count only tickers that HAVE facts.)

Insurance Brokers.reason: Commission and fee revenue. No underwriting reserves, no premiums earned, no investment float to speak of. `PremiumsEarnedNet` would resolve to nothing and the insurer top-line roll-up would return null for a company with billions in revenue.

Financial Exchanges & Data.reason: Transaction, listing and data-subscription revenue. These are Article 5 fee businesses -- MSCI and SPGI are subscription publishers that happen to be classified under Financials.

Transaction & Payment Processing Service.reason: Network and processing fees. Visa and Mastercard take no credit risk and hold no deposits; they are fee businesses with a classified balance sheet.

Asset Management & Custody Banks.reason: Management and performance fees. 'Custody Banks' in the GICS NAME is what makes this trap dangerous -- BNY and STT do take deposits and would partly fit a bank template, but BLK, TROW and the private-market managers emphatically do not, and they share the sub-industry. Routed to Article 5 as the safer uniform choice; the role-URI branch still overrides for the two custodians whenever they ship a deposit-based role, which is the correct outcome and the reason role URI is checked FIRST.

Telecom Tower REITs.reason: A tower REIT files like an infrastructure operator: classified balance sheet, cost of revenue, operating income. It is a REIT for TAX purposes, which does not change the statement shape.

Data Center REITs.reason: Same as tower REITs -- Equinix reports revenue and cost of revenue like a colocation operator.

Timber REITs.reason: Weyerhaeuser runs manufacturing segments with inventory and cost of goods sold.

mortgage_reits.measured: The plan flags mortgage REITs as classified under FINANCIALS rather than Real Estate (a real GICS property). Verified against the live roster on 2026-08-21: the S&P 500 currently contains NO mortgage-REIT sub-industry at all, so this trap has no members to mis-route today. The rule is kept so a future index addition is handled rather than silently routed to a bank template.
mortgage_reits.reason: A mortgage REIT holds a levered securities portfolio, not property. Its statements look like a securities-based operation, never like a lessor -- so neither the real_estate nor the bank template fits.
